sections.h2: What you need to sell a house in Penn Hills
sections.html:
You need an Occupancy Permit and a passing dye test before the house changes hands. Penn Hills code enforcement requires the permit for every sale, purchase or deed transfer, whether or not anyone lives in the house. It is a municipal requirement, so it applies to a cash sale as much as to a listing.

The two steps have different owners. The occupancy application goes to the Code Enforcement Department at the Government Center, 102 Duff Road, and a plumber you hire handles the dye test. Starting both early keeps them from becoming the last item standing between you and the closing table.

  • Occupancy Permit: $75 for a single family dwelling and $125 for a commercial property.
  • Dye test: the plumber of your choice runs it, files the form only after the house passes, and you submit it with a $25 filing fee.
  • Septic: a house on a septic system needs an additional septic report.

You file a three-part carbonless application, signed at the top and listing the new owner's information, and pay with it. The form posted on the municipal website is a sample and will not be accepted, so pick up the real one at the office. Payment can be cash, check or money order payable to the Municipality of Penn Hills, and cards are taken only at the office, where a service charge may apply.

If you mail the application, enclose a copy of a photo ID and name the person the inspector should meet at the property if that is not you. Inspections are scheduled Monday through Friday from 9 a.m. to 2 p.m., and the department's own hours are 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays. The same permit is needed for every change of tenant or occupant, which matters if you are selling a rental with a tenant in place.

Call Code Enforcement at (412) 342-1192 with questions. A building permit is a separate item for new construction or home improvements, so ask before you finish any repair work you started on your own.

Penn Hills sellers pay a 3% total realty transfer tax: 1.5% to the municipality, 0.5% to the Penn Hills School District and 1% to the Commonwealth. Allegheny County collects it when the deed is recorded, on a separate check from the recording fees. The sales agreement says which side pays, so price the municipal share in early.

Penn Hills is a home rule municipality in Allegheny County and one of its largest. It took home rule status in 1976. The population peaked at 62,886 in 1970 and stood at 41,059 in the 2020 census, down from 42,329 in 2010, so housing supply has outpaced demand for decades.

The municipality covers about 19 square miles, with the Allegheny River on its northern edge and Plum Creek marking the border with Plum Borough. It touches ten neighbors, among them Verona, Oakmont, Monroeville, Churchill and the Pittsburgh neighborhoods of East Hills and Lincoln-Lemington-Belmar. Neighborhood names include Lincoln Park, Milltown, Rosedale, Universal, Verona Hilltop and Frankstown Estates.

  • Middle home value is $134,700 in the 2020 to 2024 estimates, and 74.6% of households own.
  • Households: 17,964, averaging 2.23 people.
  • Median gross rent: $1,103.

Interstate 376 crosses the south end, with Penn Hills at exit 81, and Rodi Road (PA 791) connects the interstate to Frankstown Road. PA 130 and PA 380 are the other main routes. The Penn Hills School District runs Penn Hills Elementary, Linton Middle and Penn Hills High School.

Allegheny County uses base year values, and the current base year is 2012, so an assessment is not a present-day market price. The county portal lists parcels, and changes from appeals, permits and corrections post daily. The annual appeal window runs from July 1 to early September, so plan ahead if you think your value is wrong.

Penn Hills tax collection is split among the county, the municipality and the school district. Ask the county treasurer and the Penn Hills tax collector for a paid-to-date statement before you set a closing date. Anything owed at the time of sale is normally settled from the proceeds, and the title company will search for open balances.

The county runs a Homestead exclusion under Act 50 for owner-occupied homes, with the application made through the county. A buyer who will live in the house should apply in their own name after closing.

A seller must deliver a signed property disclosure statement to the buyer before the agreement of transfer is signed. The statement must address the roof, basement, structural problems, plumbing, wiring, water and sewage, drainage and other topics listed in 68 Pa.C.S. Section 7304. Several creeks run through the municipality, so the land and drainage items deserve a careful answer.

An executor or other fiduciary who sells for an estate falls outside the chapter. Everyone else owes the buyer a truthful form, and a buyer who proves a violation can recover actual damages if the suit is filed within two years after settlement. If something on the form changes before closing, tell the buyer in writing.

Run the municipal steps first, because they are the ones with set lead times. A dye test needs a plumber's schedule and an occupancy inspection needs a weekday morning or early afternoon slot. Once those are lined up, the rest is the same as anywhere: a clean title, a payoff statement and a realistic price.

  • Book the dye test and, if the house has a septic system, the septic report.
  • Pick up the carbonless occupancy form at the Government Center rather than printing the sample.
  • Cut grass before inspection; the municipality treats grass over 10 inches as high.
  • Ask Code Enforcement whether any open permits or violations are on the address.

A buyer who purchases as is still needs the municipal permit for the deed to move, so ask whether the buyer or the seller handles it and put the answer in the contract.

faqs.q: Does Penn Hills require an inspection before I sell?
faqs.a: Yes. The municipality requires an Occupancy Permit and a dye test for a sale, with an inspection scheduled on weekdays between 9 a.m. and 2 p.m. The permit is $75 for a single family home and the dye test filing fee is $25.

faqs.q: How much is the transfer tax in Penn Hills?
faqs.a: It totals 3%: 1.5% to the municipality, 0.5% to the school district and 1% to the state. Allegheny County collects it when the deed is recorded, and the sales agreement decides who pays.

faqs.q: Can I download the Penn Hills occupancy permit form online?
faqs.a: No. The form on the municipal website is only a sample and will not be accepted. Pick up the three-part carbonless form at the Code Enforcement office at 102 Duff Road, or call (412) 342-1192 about other arrangements.

faqs.q: Who does the dye test in Penn Hills?
faqs.a: A plumber of your choice does it. The plumber completes the form after the house passes, and you submit it with the $25 fee. A house on septic also needs a septic report.

faqs.q: When can I appeal my Allegheny County assessment?
faqs.a: The annual window runs from July 1 to early September. Check the county's real estate portal for the exact closing date.
